Yes, it follows that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|=\|u\|$.

**Proof.**

The norm on a Hilbert space (indeed, on any Banach space) is weakly lower semicontinuous. We use this standard fact:

> **Weak lower semicontinuity of the norm.** If $u_n \rightharpoonup u$ weakly in $H$, then
> $$\|u\| \le \liminf_{n\to\infty} \|u_n\|.$$

*Proof of the fact.* Since $u_n \rightharpoonup u$, in particular $\langle u_n, u\rangle \to \langle u, u\rangle = \|u\|^2$. By Cauchy–Schwarz,
$$|\langle u_n, u\rangle| \le \|u_n\|\,\|u\|.$$
Taking $\liminf$ of $\|u_n\|$ on the right (noting $\|u\|\ge 0$ and the left side converges to $\|u\|^2$):
$$\|u\|^2 = \lim_{n\to\infty}\langle u_n,u\rangle \le \liminf_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|\,\|u\|.$$
If $\|u\|>0$, divide by $\|u\|$ to obtain $\|u\|\le\liminf\|u_n\|$. If $\|u\|=0$, the inequality $\|u\|\le\liminf\|u_n\|$ is immediate since norms are non-negative. $\square$

Now combine the hypothesis with this fact. We are given
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|\le\|u\|,$$
and weak lower semicontinuity gives
$$\|u\|\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|.$$

Chaining these with the general inequality $\liminf \le \limsup$:
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|\;\le\;\|u\|\;\le\;\liminf_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|\;\le\;\limsup_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|.$$

All four quantities are therefore equal. In particular $\liminf\|u_n\|=\limsup\|u_n\|=\|u\|$, which means the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|$ exists and
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\|u_n\|=\|u\|.\qquad\blacksquare$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
thinking:
The problem asks: if {u_n} converges weakly to u in a Hilbert space H and limsup ||u_n|| ≤ ||u||, does it follow that lim ||u_n|| = ||u||?

This is the Kadec-Klee property / Radon-Riesz property. In Hilbert spaces, weak convergence plus convergence of norms to the norm of the limit implies strong convergence. But here we only have limsup ≤ ||u||, not equality.

Let me think. Weak convergence u_n ⇀ u. By the lower semicontinuity of norm under weak convergence, ||u|| ≤ liminf ||u_n||. Combined with limsup ||u_n|| ≤ ||u||, we get limsup ≤ ||u|| ≤ liminf. Since liminf ≤ limsup always, we have liminf = limsup = ||u||, so the limit exists and equals ||u||.

Wait, that's straightforward. Lower semicontinuity of the norm: if u_n ⇀ u, then ||u|| ≤ liminf ||u_n||. This is a standard result (norm is weakly lower semicontinuous).

So: limsup ||u_n|| ≤ ||u|| ≤ liminf ||u_n|| ≤ limsup ||u_n||. Hence equality throughout, and lim ||u_n|| = ||u||.

Yes, the answer is yes.
